args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (unhealthy, error rate 18% in us-east, us-west, eu-west). Rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging before the production deploy. v2.3.1 needs root-cause analysis before anyone redeploys it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened a SEV2 incident. The service is healthy again.

- **What went wrong:** checkout-api was running v2.3.1 in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks and 18% of requests were erroring.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production, so that's what I rolled back to. I skipped v2.3.1-rc because it only ran in staging, and it was unhealthy there too.
- **Check after rollback:** All three regions are now on v2.3.0, health checks pass, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2) is open and has paged the on-call engineer. It describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery. It also notes that the release candidate was already failing in staging, and that v2.3.1 needs its cause found before it's redeployed.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0 (v2.3.1 is unhealthy; v2.3.1-rc was staging only and unhealthy).
